scope: Scope revision 2 (2026-10-15, operational ISMS, CM-T090; revision 1 was the Phase 0 statement). The ISMS covers the design, development, operation and demonstration of the CipherMesh platform: the browser client, the API and worker, PostgreSQL and the SeaweedFS object storage as run in the local Docker Desktop demonstration and in CI, the project owner's development and operator workstation, the encrypted backups, the security evidence and ISMS records, and the management tooling (GitHub with CI, Jira Cloud) used to build it. The Oracle Cloud Always Free VM of ADR-014 is designed and enters the scope when it is provisioned; it is not deployed, and no cloud control is verified. Physical security of data centres would be the cloud provider's responsibility. People-related controls apply only in the limited sense of a one-person student project. Boundaries, interested parties and responsibilities: isms-operations.md sections 2 and 3.
statusLegend: Status values: Implemented by design (designed in Phase 0, built in the listed phase), Partial (limited by project context), Provider (responsibility transferred under shared responsibility), Not applicable.

controls.title: Policies for information security
controls.implementation: CLAUDE.md rules, security principles, invariants

controls.title: Roles and responsibilities
controls.implementation: Project roles in shared-responsibility.md; one person may hold several roles

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.implementation: Two-person approval of ADMIN invitations (PC-04); reviewer separate from author where the team allows; PLATFORM_ADMIN excluded from rooms

controls.title: Information security in project management
controls.implementation: SECURITY REVIEW status, security considerations on every backlog item

controls.title: Inventory of information and assets
controls.implementation: Asset list in the threat model (A-13, public identities, added in Phase 4), key inventory in key-hierarchy.md (identity signing key added in Phase 4), credential inventory (CM-T071)

controls.title: Classification of information
controls.implementation: STANDARD, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED profiles. Phase 10: the classification scheme is a versioned, frozen catalogue in code (no table can change a value), each room governed by its stored profile and catalogue version; handling rules PC-01 to PC-13 and PC-15 to PC-16 enforced by the API and proven by the policy matrix (PC-11 and PC-14 by plan in later phases, L-62)

controls.title: Labelling of information
controls.implementation: Profile shown on every room and in API responses. Phase 10: the room page shows the profile, the policy version and the rules the API enforces for it, read from the same catalogue

controls.title: Information transfer
controls.implementation: Client-side encrypted files, notes and secrets; TLS. Phase 7: files travel as AES-256-GCM ciphertext between the browser and object storage through short-lived presigned URLs that sign one object, one method and one size (CP-20, OL-07); the API carries only the wrapped FEK and the encrypted manifest. Phase 8: notes travel as AES-256-GCM ciphertext with a wrapped NEK; titles and bodies never leave the browser in plaintext. Phase 9: secrets travel as AES-256-GCM ciphertext with only the 32-byte SEK wrapped to the recipient's authenticated key; a burn-after-reading secret is released once and destroyed in that transaction

controls.title: Access control
controls.implementation: authorization-model.md; central room authorization module, shared matrix and route-registry enforcement built in Phase 5 (CM-T029, section 9 of the model); room lifecycle and membership routes built in Phase 5 (CM-T030, CM-T031) Phase 10: the profile access gates (PC-01, PC-02) on every room request and the PC-03 step-up for sensitive operations, in the central room authorizer and again on the locked room row (authorization model 9.11)

controls.title: Identity management
controls.implementation: Account lifecycle (registration, disabling and re-enabling with immediate session revocation), PLATFORM_ADMIN only through the server-side CLI with MFA required (built in Phase 3)

controls.title: Authentication information
controls.implementation: Argon2id with benchmarked parameters, CP-06 password policy with a breach blocklist, single-use recovery codes stored as digests, TOTP secrets encrypted at rest (built in Phase 3, authentication-security.md). Separate Vault Passphrase with its own policy, checked only in the browser and never transmitted or stored; no recovery or escrow path (built in Phase 4, ../crypto/vault.md)

controls.title: Access rights
controls.implementation: Invitations, approvals, removal with an immediate write lock and a client-driven rekey (ADR-013); access review in CM-T080. Built in Phase 5: role changes within the role ceilings, removal with the write lock, ownership transfer with a step-up, and suspension of all memberships when an account is disabled (PA-03). Built in Phase 6: invitations with role ceilings, OWNER approval of ADMIN invitations in CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED rooms (two-person rule, control 5.3), expiry set by the profile, revocation, and key delivery that is signed by the grantor and bound to the invitee's identity; the rekey follows. Built in Phase 11: leaving a room, rekeys started only by OWNER and ADMIN with one live operation, finalize only by the starter, re-sharing to a reset member under the invitation role ceilings, explicit reinstatement of a suspended member, the cryptoperiod of the profile and destruction of unused retired key versions

controls.title: Supplier relationships
controls.implementation: Provider selection ADR; Jira and GitHub treated as suppliers; shared-responsibility matrix. ICT supply chain (5.21): security libraries are selected against written criteria and reviewed (Phase 4: LIB-03 with a comparison, a code review finding and checksummed WebAssembly; LIB-05 kept in the repository)

controls.title: Information security for use of cloud services
controls.implementation: Cloud workstream (ADR-014): Oracle Cloud Always Free resources only, chosen against the criteria of service-models.md with the $0 constraint; responsibilities per component in shared-responsibility.md (IaaS VM operated by the team; PostgreSQL and SeaweedFS self-hosted on it, so their controls are the team's); provisioning gate with an explicit Always Free plan approved by the account owner (oracle-always-free.md)

controls.title: Incident management
controls.implementation: Compromise response table in the key lifecycle; Phase 11 adds the runbook for a lost or compromised identity key (../security/runbook-compromised-identity-key.md: user, administrator and operator steps, Jira security-finding record, verification table). The general incident procedure remains CM-T080

controls.title: Collection of evidence
controls.implementation: Evidence plan and redacted evidence files. Phase 14: the Trust Center evidence register lists every planned item with its status derived from the committed files and the index, missing items included. The tamper-evident audit ledger is deferred with Phase 12

controls.title: Protection of records
controls.implementation: Append-only audit table (grants and trigger, Phase 2). The hash chain and anchored checkpoints are designed (ADR-009) but deferred with Phase 12

controls.title: Privacy and protection of PII
controls.implementation: Metadata minimization, retention limits, no IP addresses in audit; metadata still visible (L-05)

controls.title: Independent review
controls.implementation: Phase 20 assessment; independence limited in a student team

controls.title: Documented operating procedures
controls.implementation: Runbooks in infrastructure/deployment

controls.title: People controls
controls.implementation: Student project context; awareness covered informally by project documentation

controls.title: Physical controls
controls.implementation: Data-centre security belongs to the cloud provider

controls.title: User endpoint devices
controls.implementation: Vault auto-lock, non-extractable keys held only in memory, no key persistence, tested in three browser engines (built in Phase 4); device security is the user's (L-01, L-38)

controls.title: Privileged access rights
controls.implementation: PLATFORM_ADMIN limits, SSH keys, database roles (four least-privilege roles and a tested grant matrix built in Phase 2, database-security.md)

controls.title: Information access restriction
controls.implementation: RBAC, object-level rules, encryption as second layer. Object-level rules (OL-01, OL-02) are proven for every room route by the BOLA and IDOR suite built in Phase 5 (CM-T032) Phase 10: access depends on the room's classification too: a session that does not meet the profile is refused every room request

controls.title: Access to source code
controls.implementation: GitHub permissions, protected main

controls.title: Secure authentication
controls.implementation: TOTP MFA, opaque server-side sessions with rotation and revocation, login backoff without lockout, CSRF defences including login CSRF, step-up (built in Phase 3). Phase 4: vault setup and passphrase change need a recent step-up, a vault reset a strict one, and a reset ends all other sessions Phase 10: the room profile decides the session requirements: MFA and a password sign-in within 4 or 1 hours (CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED), a step-up within 15 minutes for sensitive operations in RESTRICTED rooms and within 5 minutes for any downgrade

controls.title: Protection against malware
controls.implementation: Forced attachment downloads, no inline rendering, CSP; no scanning of encrypted files (L-11)

controls.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.implementation: Dependency, container and secret scanning; patching. pnpm audit:deps and gitleaks run in CI on every pull request; the dependency audit is also evidence with a 7-day freshness rule in the operational ISMS (isms-operations.md section 7)

controls.title: Configuration management
controls.implementation: Compose, Nginx, PostgreSQL, systemd and hardening configuration in Git (infrastructure/); images built only from a commit on the origin (cm-deploy), digest-pinned base images; the whole stack is built and checked on linux/arm64 in CI on every pull request

controls.title: Information deletion
controls.implementation: Expiry, burn-after-reading, crypto-shredding of live data; backup caveat (L-12)

controls.title: Data leakage prevention
controls.implementation: Client-side encryption, log redaction, encrypted filenames. Phase 7: a canary scan finds no file name or content (in four encodings) in any table, the bucket or the log, and browser tests find none in any request or browser storage (tests/files, tests/e2e/files.spec.ts). Phase 4: browser tests inspect every vault request for the passphrase in five encodings and for private-key structures, and a log test searches for every secret and ciphertext used. Phase 8: a note canary scan finds no title or body (five encodings) in any table or the log, and browser tests find none in any request or browser storage (tests/notes, tests/e2e/notes.spec.ts). Phase 9: a secret canary scan finds no text (five encodings) in any table, the log or the events, and browser tests find none in any request or browser storage (tests/secrets, tests/e2e/secrets.spec.ts)

controls.title: Information backup
controls.implementation: Cloud workstream: daily cm-backup of the database, the storage volume and the runtime secrets, encrypted with age to an offline operator key (CD-35); restore drill comparing every table digest and every file's ciphertext SHA-256 (cm-restore-drill); full restore onto an empty stack with browser decryption tested in CI (L-72)

controls.title: Logging
controls.implementation: Redacted structured application logs with the security-event catalogue; append-only audit table protection built in Phase 2; the hash chain (Phase 12) is deferred

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.implementation: Phase 14: the platform security dashboard (aggregates from the database, each with its definition, PA-01) and liveness and readiness probes. Cloud workstream: measured platform status (storage probe; host status every 5 minutes with container health, disk, memory, certificates, firewall and job outcomes), each state with its measurement time and freshness limits (T-44); the edge checker for external exposure. No alerting channel; audit verification runs are deferred with Phase 12 (L-78, L-79)

controls.title: Clock synchronization
controls.implementation: NTP synchronization on the VM checked by cm-host-setup, UTC everywhere (needed for TOTP, sessions and freshness limits)

controls.title: Network security
controls.implementation: OCI security list (22 from the operator's address, 80, 443) and host firewall (INPUT and DOCKER-USER, cm-firewall); TLS 1.2 and 1.3 at the edge (CP-21) and TLS 1.3 with verify-full on the database hop (CD-34)

controls.title: Security of network services
controls.implementation: PostgreSQL: TLS-only runtime roles (hostssl), no superuser network login; object storage: signed object requests of one bucket only, cookies refused, IAM API off, one identity limited to that bucket

controls.title: Segregation of networks
controls.implementation: Four Docker networks: edge (Nginx only), and internal app, data and storage networks without egress; the database and the storage are reachable only from the containers that need them

controls.title: Use of cryptography
controls.implementation: docs/crypto/ and the parameter register. Phase 4: packages/crypto with narrow interfaces and known-answer tests from published sources, browser Argon2id selected by benchmark (ADR-010), identity signing keys decided before implementation (ADR-015), a specified vault format (../crypto/vault.md). Phase 6: room keys generated in the browser, envelopes bound to room, version, user and key, a signed commitment and signed statements verified before any key is used (ADR-015 section 4.1), ADR-007 accepted after a cross-engine test, the Room Safety Code word list selected by written criteria (LIB-08). Phase 11: browser-made rekeyed versions chained by signed statements, the wrap limit and the cryptoperiod, and an engine finding with its fix (SF-11-01, CD-33) found by cross-browser testing

controls.title: Secure development life cycle
controls.implementation: Workflow, Definition of Done, phase gates

controls.title: Application security requirements
controls.implementation: Invariants, policy profiles, ASVS target

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.implementation: Security principles, ADRs, trust boundaries

controls.title: Secure coding
controls.implementation: Coding conventions, forbidden-API lint rules. Phase 4: no cryptographic function accepts an IV, an algorithm or a raw AAD; the export surface and the test-only seam are fixed by a test; browser code may not import crypto internals (lint)

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.implementation: security-testing-plan.md. Phase 4: 17 more negative controls (27 in total, five of them in a real browser), a 90% coverage gate for packages/crypto in CI, and cross-engine browser tests; security finding SF-04-01 fixed with a regression test that failed before the fix

controls.title: Separation of environments
controls.implementation: Local development, CI and the local rehearsal use their own throwaway credentials; the cloud's secrets are generated on the VM and never used elsewhere; synthetic data only

controls.title: Change management
controls.implementation: Jira workflow plus pull requests; database changes only as reviewed migrations, with destructive Prisma commands refused and a drift check in CI (Phase 2). Phase 4: the cryptographic design change (OCD-12) was decided in an ADR and accepted by the project owner before any code was written; the identity migration fails rather than altering existing rows Phase 10: a policy value changes only through a reviewed pull request and a new catalogue version; profile changes are OWNER-only, recorded as events, downgrades with high severity

controls.title: Test information
controls.implementation: Synthetic data only: the seed uses reserved .test addresses, disabled accounts, no credentials and no key material (Phase 2)
